articles.title: Norris leva a pole no GP de São Paulo; Bortoleto e Câmara batem | Ge
articles.standfirst: Britânico sairá na frente pelo 3º ano seguido em Interlagos. Rafa Câmara e Gabriel Bortoleto colidem com muro em momentos diferentes do treino e largarão em 11º e 19º, respectivamente
articles.summary: Britânico sairá na frente pelo 3º ano seguido em Interlagos. Câmara e Bortoleto colidem com muro em momentos diferentes do treino e largarão em 11º e 19º, respectivamente
articles.body:
Desde que chegaram ao Brasil, alguns pilotos já anunciavam: o clima em Interlagos é sempre uma incógnita e pode interferir no andamento do fim de semana. Neste sábado (7), ainda nos primeiros minutos do Q1, a classificação para o GP de São Paulo de Fórmula 1 foi interrompida por chuva forte, que dificultava a visibilidade na pista e fazia os carros aquaplanarem. A sessão ficou paralisada por 1h24min, até que o dilúvio desse trégua. Com o treino retomado, emoção não faltou. Lando Norris, da McLaren, garantiu a terceira pole position seguida em Interlagos, em um Q3 marcado novamente pelo tempo ruim. Os brasileiros Rafael Câmara (Haas) e Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) bateram em momentos diferentes da atividade. Largarão em 11º e 19º, respectivamente – posições definidas por punições a outros pilotos.

A corrida principal do GP de São Paulo de Fórmula 1 terá transmissão ao vivo da TV Globo, neste domingo (8), a partir de 13h30 (de Brasília). O sportv3 também exibirá a prova, assim como o ge, que ainda acompanhará tudo em tempo real .

Campeão mundial em 2025, Norris fez o melhor tempo do Q1 e continuou com bom ritmo nas sessões seguintes. Quando a chuva voltou a ficar forte no Q3, o britânico era quem tinha conseguido a volta mais rápida e se beneficiou do fato de a pista molhada impedir que outros pilotos melhorassem suas marcas. Com a pole position assegurada, Lando se junta a um seleto grupo de corredores que largaram na frente em Interlagos por três anos seguidos. Só Felipe Massa e Mika Häkkinen tinham alcançado o feito.

Lando Norris, pole position do GP de São Paulo de 2026 — Foto: Amanda Perobelli - Reuters

Na primeira classificação da carreira na Fórmula 1, o estreante Câmara rodou no Q1, furou um pneu e danificou a asa dianteira, mas teve tempo de consertar o carro. O brasileiro voltou à pista, melhorou seu tempo e avançou à etapa seguinte do treino. No Q2, o jovem de 21 anos vinha em volta rápida, que podia colocá-lo entre os 10 mais velozes. Contudo, perdeu o controle do carro em uma curva e foi direto para o muro de Interlagos. Chateado com a batida e a eliminação em 13º, Rafa pediu desculpas à equipe pelo rádio.

Rafael Câmara na classificação do GP de São Paulo da F1 2026 — Foto: MIGUEL SCHINCARIOL / AFP

Outro representante do Brasil em Interlagos, Bortoleto reviveu um drama de 2025. No ano passado, o piloto, então na Sauber, bateu ainda na primeira volta do GP de São Paulo. Neste sábado, Gabriel chegou com a moral de quem teve bom rendimento nos treinos livres, mas acabou prejudicado pela chuva, rodou e colidiu com um muro em tentativa de volta rápida. Com danos na asa traseira, não voltou mais à pista e foi eliminado no Q1, registrando o pior tempo da sessão.

Apesar das batidas, Câmara e Bortoleto ganharam posições no grid, visto que os resultados da classificação foram influenciados por penalizações a alguns pilotos. Max Verstappen, Sergio Pérez e Lewis Hamilton já sabiam que partiriam do fim da fila, devido a alterações em componentes dos motores. Charles Leclerc perdeu 10 posições, enquanto George Russell caiu cinco colocações, também por mudanças em seus carros.

*Pilotos que perderam posições devido a alterações em seus carros.

Grid de largada do GP de São Paulo de Fórmula 1 — Foto: Reprodução/FIA

A chuva chegou com força minutos antes de os carros iniciarem o Q1. De última hora, algumas equipes optaram por trocar os pneus intermediários e colocar compostos para pista molhada. Mas a visibilidade rapidamente ficou comprometida, e pilotos começaram a aquaplanar antes mesmo de abrir volta. Por isso, a Fórmula 1 anunciou bandeira vermelha e suspendeu a sessão sem nenhum tempo registrado.

Chuva em Interlagos interrompe classificação — Foto: REUTERS/Adriano Machado

A atividade só foi retomada 1h24min depois, ainda com água na pista. Todos os pilotos saíram com pneus para chuva forte, e as posições na tabela de tempos mudavam a todo instante. Rafael Câmara, em seu primeiro GP de F1 na carreira, rodou no início da sessão, mas conseguiu recolocar o carro na pista e se recuperou, avançando ao Q2 com o 13º melhor tempo.

Gabriel Bortoleto sofreu com a água na pista e bateu no muro da subida da Junção. A pancada danificou a asa traseira do carro da Audi, e o brasileiro não retornou mais à pista. Assim, ficou com o pior tempo do Q1, sendo eliminado e revivendo o trauma de 2025, quando abandonou o GP ainda na primeira volta, depois de uma colisão.

Gabriel Bortoleto na classificação do GP de São Paulo de F1 — Foto: Reuters

Franco Colapinto, Pierre Gasly, Lance Stroll, Valtteri Bottas e Sergio Pérez também não avançaram ao Q2. Lando Norris ficou com o melhor tempo da primeira parte da classificação.

17º Franco Colapinto (Alpine) 18º Pierre Gasly (Alpine) 19º Lance Stroll (Aston Martin) 20º Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) 21º Sergio Pérez (Cadillac) 22º Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi)

Ciente da punição que o jogava para o fim do grid, Max Verstappen nem entrou na pista, e Arvid Lindblad teve problemas com o carro. O Q2, que também tinha trocas na liderança, foi encerrado devido à batida de Rafael Câmara. O brasileiro vinha em volta rápida, com chances de melhorar o tempo, mas saiu reto de uma curva e parou no muro. Com isso, acabou eliminado, assim como Hamilton, Oscar Piastri, Lindblad e Verstappen.

Rafael Câmara a caminho dos boxes após bater na classificação do GP de São Paulo de F1 — Foto: PH Peixoto

George Russell fez o melhor tempo do Q2 (1min27s049).

11º Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) 12º Oscar Piastri (McLaren) 13º Rafael Câmara (Haas) 14º Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) 15º Carlos Sainz (Williams) 16º Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

A última parte da classificação também durou menos que o esperado. A chuva voltou a apertar, e, com a pista bastante molhada, os pilotos nem tentaram voltas nos últimos minutos do cronômetro. Lando Norris foi quem se beneficiou. O britânico da McLaren, campeão mundial em 2025, fez a volta mais rápida e assegurou a terceira pole position seguida em Interlagos.

Lando Norris na classificação do GP de São Paulo da F1 2026 — Foto: Amanda Perobelli/REUTERS

George Russell ficou com a segunda posição, mas largará em sétimo, punido por trocar componentes do motor. Por isso, Kimi Antonelli completará a primeira fila do grid de largada.

Charles Leclerc, quarto colocado, partirá da 14ª posição. Como consequência, Liam Lawson e Nico Hulkenberg estarão na terceira e quarta posições do grid, respectivamente.

articles.title: Quiles, pole de casi récord en Moto3 pese a sus caídas
articles.standfirst: Pudo con Almansa, Brian Uriarte y Carpe
articles.summary: Pudo con Almansa, Brian Uriarte y Carpe
articles.body: Máximo Quiles logró la pole de Moto3 del Gran Premio de Qatar, en Lusail. El ya campeón rozó el récord y ni apretó al final. Sólo David Almansa se le arrimó algo. El calor era alto, aunque ya estaba anocheciendo, con 33 grados en el ambiente hasta 43 en el asfalto. En el comienzo de la Q1, destacaba la presencia de los dos del Ajo KTM, Carpe y Brian Uriarte, que pelean por el subcampeonato. El murciano partía primero, sin importarle que muchos buscaran su rueda. Carpe se iba largo en el primer intento y no cuadraba el siguiente. Brian tenía que adelantar a otros competidores, pero fijaba un crono mejor. Pini, en el grupo, tomaba la cabeza. Para la última salida, Álvaro volvía a salir a liderar el grupo. Ríos se pegaba a él y Uriarte ahora dejaba más metros. Se lo jugaron a una sola vuelta y Carpe lo salvó. El cántabro se permitió endosar medio segundo al siguiente. Pasaron: Uriarte, Mitani, Carpe y O’Gorman. En la segunda parte de la parrilla formarán: 19. Pini, 20. Ríos, 21. Singhapong, 22. Rammerstorfer, 23. Moodley, 24. Cruces y 25. Mononyane. En el inicio de la Q2, uno de los puntos clave era ver cómo estaba de confianza Quiles, tras sus dos fuertes caídas en los entrenamientos previos. El murciano, que celebrará el título en su ciudad el sábado que viene, partía el primero. Los del Ajo esperaban a Almansa para ir tras él. El manchego tomaba la cabeza, aunque Máximo apretaba para dejar de rueda a los que le perseguían, Adrián Fernández y David Muñoz. El pupilo de Aspar elevaba el listón, quedándose a 12 milésimas de batir el récord de Dani Holgado. Almansa trató de replicar, pero le faltó una décima, lo que perdió en el sector final; David ya había hecho el giro solo, pues Brian y Álvaro ya se habían ido a su garaje. Todos esperaron muchísimo para retornar a la acción. De hecho, Quiles hacía un amago y se quedaba más, como Almansa. Los dos partieron tan tarde que no tenían tiempo para realizar un giro a tope, como Carpe, que los aguardó. Adrián Fernández podía haberse convertido en la amenaza, pues iba rebajando en una décima el mejor tiempo, pero el madrileño se encontró tráfico. Así, Uriarte era el que mejor rendimiento sacaba a esta vuelta para escalar al tercer lugar. ‘Top 6’ pleno de españoles. Eso sí, la pole era para Quiles, que la hizo sin forzar al final. Y eso que era la primera vez que competía en Lusail. "Tuve caídas grandes y eso hizo que diera un paso atrás para calmarme un poco. Doy gracias al equipo por rehacerme la moto", decía Máximo.

articles.title: Marc Márquez gana y puede ser campeón en Qatar, pese a un heroico Jorge Martín
articles.standfirst: Toque entre Marc y Bezzecchi y el italiano, al suelo
articles.summary: Toque entre Marc y Bezzecchi y el italiano, al suelo
articles.body: Marc Márquez ganó el Sprint de MotoGP del Gran Premio de Qatar, en Lusail. El ilerdense puede ser campeón este domingo si vence la carrera larga y Martinator no puntúa. Es la única cuenta que le da la corona. Todo porque Jorge Martín fue tercero tras una heroica remontada. La polémica estuvo en el toque entre Marc y Bezzecchi. Tan sólo compitieron 18 pilotos, pues son baja los cuatro de Yamaha: Quartararo, Rins, Miller y Augusto Fernández. Dixon suple a Mir, en el Honda oficial, y Lecuona a Álex Márquez, en el Gresini Ducati. Hacía menos calor al caer ya la noche, con 29 grados en el ambiente y 35 en el asfalto. Las Aprilia y el resto iban con goma media trasera y sólo las Ducati de Marc y ‘Diggia’, con blanda. En la salida, Bezzecchi cerraba el interior a Marc para aguantar en el ángulo inicial. Bagnaia metía la moto a su compañero, pero el ‘93’ replicaba al momento. Di Giannantonio también rebasaba a Pecco. Las dos Trackhouse tenían un contacto leve, del que salía bien librado Raúl, que superaba a Bagnaia antes de pasar por primera vez por meta. Aldeguer quiso rebasar a Acosta, pero se pasó algo de frenada y tocó con su parte delantera a la trasera de Bagnaia. El turinés voló de forma fea. Fermín resistió, pero bajó al último lugar. Los comisarios anunciaron una investigación. ‘Bez’ tiraba muy fuerte y Marc aguantaba a duras penas. Raúl superaba a ‘Diggia’, pero al llegar de nuevo a la curva 16, los comisarios estaban retirando a Bagnaia en camilla, aunque consciente, y su Ducati. Por eso, la Dirección de Carrera sacó la bandera roja y paró la prueba. La nueva carrera iba a ser a sólo diez vueltas, una menos, con las mismas posiciones de la parrilla original. Martín cambiaba y ponía una goma blanda nueva trasera; Marc mantenía un blando nuevo atrás, Bezzecchi dejaba sus compuestos medios gastados y ‘Diggia’ se pasaba al medio trasero. Aldeguer era penalizado con pasar dos veces por la zona de la ‘Long Lap’ por el toque a Pecco. En la segunda salida, Marc superaba a Bezzecchi. Raúl había arrancado bien, pero el dispositivo para bajar la moto se le quedaba enganchado y le pasaban ‘Diggia’ y Zarco. Martín crecía del undécimo al séptimo. Jorge se sentía mejor con este neumático y rebasaba a Acosta con facilidad. Luego, en la recta, se lanzó a pasar a Raúl y lo logró en la zona de la 2-3, cuando Fernández levantó algo. ‘Bez’ inició una ofensiva sobre Marc, pero el de Cervera resistió. Martinator pasaba a Zarco al encarar de nuevo la recta y ya era cuarto, excelente. Quién diría que tenía un hueso roto en su muñeca derecha. Bezzecchi intentó superar al mayor de los Márquez, quien para aguantar se coló un poco. Al volver al vértice de la curva 1, se tocaron y Marco se fue al suelo; a Marc se le activó el ‘airbag’, pero resistió sobre su GP26. Los comisarios dictaminaron que no había sanción y en Aprilia no se lo creían. Casi a la vez, Martinator rebasaba a ‘Diggia’. Para sorpresa de muchos, Jorge adelantaba a Marc, pero el del Ducati oficial respondía al momento. Raúl, Zarco y Acosta se enzarzaban en una pelea por el cuarto lugar. A falta de cinco vueltas, el vigente campeón hacía la vuelta rápida y se marchaba medio segundo. ‘Diggia’ buscaba un hueco para adelantar a Martín. Poco a poco, el ‘93’ se iba fugando y la opción de que pudiera ser campeón este domingo en Lusail dependía de si Di Giannantonio adelantaba a Jorge. El romano logró pasar en la curva 2, tras tomar el exterior en el primer ángulo. Martinator ya no pudo replicar, porque el del VR46 cerró muy bien. La victoria de Marc le da la opción de atar ya el título este domingo en Qatar. Es difícil, pero no imposible.

articles.body:
Última hora de la calificación en Interlagos

Kimi Antonelli se perfila como el gran favorito para la pole y para lucir su flamante título Mundial conseguido la semana pasada en México, pero deberá confirmarlo en una jornada en la que amenaza lluvia constante sobre el circuito de Interlagos. El piloto de Mercedes fue el segundo en los libres 3 sólo por detrás de Verstappen , que está penalizado para la carrera del domingo por cambio de motor.

Los Ferrari , tras la reunión para pacificar la última trifulca entre Leclerc y Hamilton , no parecen de inicio entre los mejores y más después de los 10 puestos de penalización que tiene el monegasco y los más de 35 para Lewis por cambier la unidad completa. Sólo Norris o Piastri parecen rivales para Kimi, pues Russell también tiene 5 puestos de sanción.

En cuanto a los españoles, el 18º de Alonso y el 19º de Sainz en libres 3 no hacen augurar un buen resultados para ambos, pero la lluvia que está cayendo en Interlagos puede cambiarlo todo.

articles.title: Marc Márquez califica el toque como "error de Bezzecchi"
articles.standfirst: Cree que no será campeón este domingo
articles.summary: Cree que no será campeón este domingo
articles.body: Marc Márquez estaba feliz por su victoria en el Sprint de MotoGP del Gran Premio de Qatar, en Lusail. Eso sí, el vigente campeón era cauto respecto a sus opciones de ser campeón este mismo domingo en el trazado qatarí, donde sólo le vale ganar y que Jorge Martín no sume. El del Ducati oficial daba su opinión sobre el toque con Bezzecchi en DAZN. “Lo primero, esperemos que Pecco no tenga nada grave y esté bien, pero esta bandera roja ha cambiado los planes de todos, incluso algunos han cambiado los neumáticos. En la primera carrera, me encontraba muy bien; Bezzecchi tiraba, pero iba bien, me hubiera ganado, porque tenía más ritmo. En la segunda, al salir bien y ponerme primero, he defendido con todo, como hice en Australia para intentar estar liderando la carrera las máximas vueltas posibles. Son muy importantes estos 12 puntos”. “Me ha sorprendido mucho el encontrarlo ahí dentro, porque yo no he hecho nada raro, he hecho mi línea, que cada vuelta era ésa: frenas, vas un poco largo y vuelves. Creo que él tenía un extra de velocidad, que mañana lo va a demostrar en carrera, e incluso he estado a punto de caer, he hecho 4 ó 5 curvas con el ‘airbag’ encendido del toque y ahí he dicho: ‘Ahora nos calmamos’, pero he visto que me atacaba Martín. Eso no me lo esperaba, ahí me ha descolocado todo. Dije: ‘Venga, ahora toca apretar’. Cuando he visto a Martín cerca ya he dicho: ‘Tengo que quedar por delante de él sí o sí’. Es ahí donde he intentado imponer un ritmo para abrir la distancia y mantenerla”. “Creo que Martín, viendo los entrenamientos, estará ahí. Quizá el ‘time attack’ (intento a una vuelta9 es lo que le ha costado más, pero de ritmo está muy parecido al mío. El que está por delante claramente es Bezzecchi. Veremos. Di Giannantonio también está muy bien, pero, evidentemente, con el error de Bezzecchi de hoy, la prioridad es quedar por delante de Martín, una posición por delante o dos, da igual, o una posición por detrás. Este será el objetivo principal”. “Mañana no toca. Tengo ganas, ¿eh? Y soy el primero que quiere cerrarlo lo antes posible, pero hoy estos 12 han sido regalados, entre comillas; los buscas, los trabajas, pero no tenía el ritmo para conseguirlos. ¿Cómo? Se han sacado. Mañana, tenemos que ser realistas, 25 no tocaría, pero veremos, salimos a carrera sin descartar nada”.

articles.title: Pecco Bagnaia, con varias fracturas tras un feo accidente
articles.standfirst: Toque de Fermín Aldeguer y vuelo
articles.summary: Toque de Fermín Aldeguer y vuelo
articles.body: Pecco Bagnaia sufrió un fuerte accidente en el comienzo de la carrera al Sprint de MotoGP del Gran Premio de Qatar, en Lusail. El italiano había remontado en los giros iniciales e incluso se llegó a poner segundo tras adelanta a su compañero Marc Márquez, pero, luego, el turinés fue perdiendo comba. Así, el de Chivasso iba circulando en el grupo cuando Fermín Aldeguer intentó adelantar a Pedro Acosta, pero el del Gresini se coló algo y tocó con la parte delantera de su moto a la trasera de Bagnaia. El tricampeón hizo palanca y voló varios metros, impactando de forma violenta contra el asfalto de la escapatoria. Pecco quedó tendido en el suelo, aunque, rápidamente, se informó que estaba consciente. Tras sacar la bandera roja la Dirección de Carrera, se paró la prueba y Bagnaia fue evacuado en camilla a una ambulancia que lo trasladó a la clínica del circuito. Allí, el doctor Ángel Charte certificó que tiene dos fracturas en el pie derecho, en el cuarto y el quinto dedo. Hay que operar las dos, según informaron los médicos. El del Ducati oficial fue trasladado a un hospital en Doha, donde le harán más pruebas. Es baja para la carrera larga de este domingo. Los comisarios impusieron una sanción de pasar dos veces por la zona de la 'Long Lap' a Aldeguer durante el parón. El de La Ñora, después, se excusó. "Pedir disculpas a Pecco y Ducati. Son cosas que no quieres que pasen. Poco ha pasado para lo que podía haber sido", indicó en DAZN. Pedro Acosta, que estaba en ese lance, dio su opinión. "Un movimiento muy agresivo para ser muy pronto en la carrera. Son errores que pueden pasar. Vuelve después de la lesión, un error lo tiene cualquiera", dijo en DAZN.

articles.title: Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Lando Norris claims rain-hit pole in wild conditions with Lewis Hamilton, Max Verstappen to start at back
articles.summary: Lando Norris tames awful wet conditions for his third Brazil pole in a row; Frustrated Russell drops down from second with grid penalty; Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen starting 20th and 21st; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo GP live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm
articles.body:
On a typically rain-hit day at ever-unpredictable Interlagos, qualifying was suspended for over an hour and 20 minutes after a torrential downpour hit the drivers' first laps of Q1.

The rain eventually eased - but never particularly stopped - to allow running take place and create a thrilling and unpredictable battle for pole.

In the end it was Norris who came out ahead as conditions worsened again in Q3 to seal a third successive Interlagos pole position for the outgoing world champion, on a weekend McLaren had already showed improved form in the dry following car upgrades.

Mercedes' George Russell was second fastest ahead of a race he already knew he carries a five-place grid penalty for an engine change, meaning he could not ultimately achieve pole position whatever he did.

He lapped 0.204s slower than Norris and from second will drop to seventh on Sunday's grid.

But the Mercedes driver was left frustrated not to have topped the qualifying timesheet outright, which he believes he would have done had he not been advised by his race engineer to back out of what turned out to be his final representative timed lap of Q3 when he came up behind Alex Albon's slower Williams.

Russell's engineer, Marcus Dudley, clearly hoped this would pay dividends by giving the Briton a clearer run on his next lap but the call coincided with the rain increasing again, meaning lap times quickly became slower.

Drivers swiftly headed back to the pit lane to mark an effective end to the Q3 battle as they all stayed in the garage as the clock ticked down to zero.

"I don't want to be P2. I want to be P1!" fumed Russell on team radio at the end of the session.

New world champion Kimi Antonelli qualified third but will move ahead of team-mate Russell to the front row alongside Norris.

Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari but he has a 10-place penalty for an engine change to serve so will drop down into the midfield.

His team-mate Hamilton was also originally supposed to serve the same sanction but a problem with his fresh Ferrari engine in final practice triggered a complete power-unit change and locked him in to a back-of-the-grid start.

He will be joined on the back rows by old title rival Verstappen, who has also taken a new power unit in his Red Bull from Saturday's running.

Both drivers dropped out in Q2, Hamilton in 11th and Verstappen in 16th after opting not to run in the second phase at all in order to save wet tyres for the race, but neither result mattered given their overriding penalties.

Ferrari's heavier grid penalties increase Mercedes' chances of closing out the Constructors' Championship on Sunday. They will complete a title double for 2026 if they outscore their Italian rivals by three points or more.

Front-running penalties promote midfield runners up grid

The grid penalties for Russell, Verstappen and both Ferraris - which were all confirmed in the sessions ahead of qualifying - mean Sunday's grid has a different complexion to normal in a season dominated by the 'big four' teams.

Russell and Leclerc's demotions move Liam Lawson - whose future at Racing Bulls remain in huge doubt despite his impressive season - to a joint career-best third on the grid after the New Zealander already impressed in the wet to qualify fifth.

There were also strong performances in the rain from Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, who will start fourth, and Haas' Oliver Bearman, who will line up sixth. With Verstappen at the back, Isack Hadjar will be the lead Red Bull driver in fifth.

Fernando Alonso showed his old mastery of the rain to put under-powered Aston Martin into Q3 for the first time this season, while Williams' Alex Albon also made his first top-10 appearance of a difficult year.

Alonso and Albon will line up in eighth and ninth respectively.

That is just ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri - after he dropped out in Q2 - and Brazilian debutant Rafael Camara in 11th.

Haas' new signing hugely impressed on his F1 debut to make Q2 before blotting his copybook slightly by crashing into the barriers at the end of that second phase.

Arvid Lindblad will line up 12th after his Racing Bulls car was stopped by technical issues in Q2.

articles.title: Sao Paulo Grand Prix: Lando Norris takes pole after rain-delayed qualifying
articles.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris takes pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in a wet qualifying session at Interlagos delayed by nearly an hour and a half for heavy rain.
articles.body:
McLaren's Lando Norris took pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix in a wet qualifying session at Interlagos delayed by nearly an hour and a half for heavy rain.

Norris beat fellow Briton George Russell by 0.204 seconds, and the Mercedes driver was fuming that he could have been faster had he not been told by his engineer to abort a faster lap before the rain became heavier.

In any case, Russell has a five-place grid penalty for exceeding his permitted number of engine parts, promoting team-mate and new world champion Kimi Antonelli to second.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc qualified fourth but has a 10-place grid penalty which promotes Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson to third.

The New Zealander was one of a number of drivers to have their best qualifying session of the year thanks to the levelling effect of the wet weather.

Also among them were Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, who qualified sixth and will start fourth, Haas driver Oliver Bearman, who was eighth and will start sixth, and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso, who was ninth and will move up one place to eighth, plus Wlliams' Alex Albon, who is right behind Alonso.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was knocked out in Q2 but will start 10th because of the penalties, while Brazilian Rafael Camara will line up 11th on his F1 debut, despite crashing his Haas towards the end of the second session.

Hamilton & Verstappen to start from back in Brazil

Qualifying started at 15:00 local time but was stopped before anyone could set a lap because the conditions were too dangerous to continue.

Bearman said: "Definitely the wettest conditions I've experienced in a race car, if not any car, and that's saying a lot given I grew up in the UK."

It was finally restarted again an hour and 26 minutes after the originally scheduled start time.

And a plethora of engine-related grid penalties changed the shape of qualifying as Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who was third fastest in the first session, did not take part in the second because he knew he would be starting at the back of the grid.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton, who also starts from the back for the same reason, did take part in the second session but also saved his tyres for the race and qualified 11th.

The rain gave an opportunity for drivers in usually uncompetitive cars to shine, chief among them Alonso, whose Aston Martin has been among the slowest cars in the field all season.

The veteran Spanish two-time world champion was in the running among the leaders throughout the session but even in the wet the lack of power from the Honda engine meant he still faced a handicap.

But it was Norris who shone brightest. The 2025 world champion has looked quick all weekend in the upgraded McLaren. He repeated his pole from Brazil last year, and will start from the front for the first time since the Spanish Grand Prix in September.

Norris said: "It's been a long day, a great qualifying. It was about getting two laps in at the beginning and not making mistakes and that's what we did."

Russell was still ruing the decision not to complete his final lap, saying: "Congrats to Lando. That was definitely the pole lap. The rain was coming and we should have just finished the lap. Felt more confident in the wet than we did in the dry."

2. George Russell (Mercedes) - five-place grid penalty

4. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) - 10-place grid penalty

articles.title: Alonso obra el milagro y Norris sorprende a los Mercedes en el diluvio
articles.standfirst: El británico de McLaren firma la mejor pole position del curso (1:27.470) en una sesión de clasificación pasada por agua
articles.summary: El británico de McLaren firma la mejor pole position del curso (1:27.470) en una sesión de clasificación pasada por agua
articles.body: Nada se compara a la lluvia. Es el elemento capaz de reventar todos los pronósticos, eleva a los pilotos de verdad y disminuye el gran efecto de las máquinas. Y pese que el pilotaje bajo el agua es cada vez más extraño en una Fórmula 1 conservadora por norma, si aparece todo mejora. Ocurrió en la clasificación del Gran Premio de Brasil y resultó el mejor espectáculo de la temporada. Uno en el que Fernando Alonso hizo magia y metió al Aston Martin en la Q3 para salir octavo y que tiene a Lando Norris al frente con el campeón Antonelli a su lado en la salida del domingo (18:00 horas, DAZN). Que competir bajo la lluvia iba a ser un asunto delicado se sabía desde el inicio y se constató con los pocos minutos de Q1 disputados. Varios coches salieron, el aquaplanning fue total y la bandera roja cayó. "Han sido las peores condiciones en las que he pilotado estos coches", radiografiaba Oliver Bearman, piloto de Haas. Que lo llevaba más allá. "O cualquier coche... y eso que soy británico", agregó. Nadie pudo rodar durante 84 minutos, pero la sesión pudo comenzar. Con pequeños golpes de Bortoleto y Camara como sustos serios. Y si llovía, los españoles sonreían. Especialmente Fernando Alonso, que firmó su mejor sábado de la temporada. Llegó a comandar testimonialmente la Q1 y pasó a la Q3 tras un segundo corte que dinamitó un golpe de Cámara en la curva 12. Por primera vez, el asturiano ponía al AMR26 en un lugar que no pertenece por rendimiento. Pero la lluvia cambia todo. Y el bicampeón pudo rascar un noveno que se convierte en octavo por las sanciones. Decidió lanzarse en cabeza en el último intento, sus intermedios carburaron y tiene una oportunidad de sumar. Siempre y cuando las condiciones se mantengan y la lluvia pueda disminuir un déficit del motor Honda que sigue. En el inicio y final del circuito no hay paz para el Aston, pero Alonso consigue hacerse fuerte en el incómodo pilotaje cuando hay la mínima oportunidad. En Brasil, una de sus mecas, ya tiene el mejor día a una vuelta de todo el 2026. Carlos Sainz también aprovechó la lluvia. No sin sustos, pues para certificar el pase de la Q1 tuvo que pasar un trompo en la última frenada y un sector intermedio en el que su Williams era un potro salvaje. Pero salvó ese corte, aunque no consiguió entrar en el top-10 al que sí accedió Albon. En una de sus vueltas tuvo otra pequeña salida y no fue capaz de mejorar tras la bandera roja del fin de la Q2. Eso sí, las sanciones le hacen subir hasta el puesto 13. Porque, precisamente, los castigos también mezclan la baraja de cara a la carrera. Hay penalización a Verstappen al cambiar el motor y partirá penúltimo (21º). También a Lewis Hamilton, que lo hará 20º. Y llegan a afectar en menor medida a George Russell, cayendo al séptimo desde el segundo y Charles Leclerc, obligado a partir desde la casilla 14. El tiempo bien puede darles una oportunidad... o abrir el camino a los de cabeza. Que serán, de nuevo, Norris y Antonelli. El británico certificó el resurgir de McLaren por velocidad e inteligencia, cosa que marcó al poder firmar dos vueltas antes del diluvio de la Q3. Y sumó un error en Mercedes, que pidió a Russell no tirar cuando tenía la ventana. "Tenía que haber cerrado esa vuelta, hemos ejecutado mal", se lamentaba el británico. Su penalización abre el paso a Antonelli, que salvó los muebles con un buen lugar de partida. Como el que también tiene la segunda línea más sorprendente de la temporada. Corresponderá a un enorme Liam Lawson, tercero y reivindicando su lugar en la Fórmula 1. Y a Nico Hülkenberg, muy solvente en un Audi que sí funcionó en condiciones adversas. Mandarán en los coches de esa segunda división que sueña con más lío para poder dar el gran golpe. Suya es una oportunidad de oro tras el mejor sábado de toda la temporada. La lluvia siempre es bienvenida.

articles.title: Josh Berry regrets Ryan Blaney brake check, expected NASCAR penalty
articles.summary: He said he was 'screwed' the moment Hocevar retaliated on Cindric
articles.body:
With nothing else to gain from denying it to the media like what happened immediately after the race at Martinsville on Sunday, Josh Berry admitted to brake checking Ryan Blaney out of contention, and expressed remorse for his actions.

Berry was issued a $50,000 fine with the loss of 25 driver points by NASCAR earlier in the week.

"First and foremost, I regret the decision I made in the heat of the moment there," Berry said. "Obviously, looking back on it, Ryan had caught up to me. I was stuck behind ( Bubba Wallace ) for a little bit and Ryan got to me.

"He peaked out a little bit into (Turn 3) and he got into me in the center of (Turns) 3 and 4 and I just overreacted to it. The contact just rubbed me the wrong way and I got upset and I made a bad decision in that moment that I regret and obviously wish I'd have made a better decision there, but just really can't change nothing about it now."

He started to make amends before the night even ended on Sunday given that the Wood Brothers No. 21 that he drives for at least one more weekend is aligned with Team Penske .

"I spoke to him on Sunday night," Berry said. "We weren't even in Statesville yet, I don't think before I talked to him. I talked to him, I talked to Roger (Penske) talked to (crew chief) Jonathan Hassler or left Hassler voicemail, and then he got back to me the next day.

"So yeah, I felt like I did all I could to at least let him know where I stood on it, that I regretted the decision that I made and was upset with myself for making that decision. And that was really all I could do in that moment."

Berry said he doesn't expect Blaney to forgive him 'overnight' but he also doesn't expect anything else to come from it. He also knew he was 'screwed' the moment he realized that Hocevar had brake checked Austin Cindric four times until the car received terminal damage.

"As egregious as his was, I felt like it was two totally different situations and obviously mine was reacting to the contact I got from behind, a one-and-done kind of deal," Berry said. "As many attempts as he had made to put the two out of the race and finally succeeding, I knew that I was probably going to get something related and obviously that's what ended up happening."

Taylor Kitchen contributed to this report

articles.title: Alonso quiere más tras su mejor sábado: "Creía que el top-5 era posible"
articles.standfirst: El asturiano saldrá octavo tras firmar la mejor clasificación de todo el curso 2026
articles.summary: El asturiano saldrá octavo tras firmar la mejor clasificación de todo el curso 2026
articles.body: Fernando Alonso firmó su mejor sábado de toda la temporada 2026. No es un octavo puesto en parrilla de salida un lugar soñado, pero es más que válido atendiendo a un año con sólo siete puntos en el casillero y los innumerables problemas del Aston Martin AMR26. Llegó en una de las señas de identidad del asturiano, el pilotaje en agua. Atacó, entró en la Q3 e incluso creyó que su oportunidad era mejor que la cuarta fila de inicio al domingo. "En la Q3 esperaba más al ser el primero de la cola. Pero las ruedas estaban congeladas y no tenía grip", comentó ante la prensa internacional. Su estimación era mucho más optimista. "Creía que el top-5 era posible. Pero las ruedas no tenían agarre en la primera vuelta y pensé en atacar en la segunda. Pero me quedé sin energía por los modos del motor, así que terminé en tierra de nadie. La primera vuelta no era buena para las gomas, la segunda por el motor. Creo que habría medio segundo o ocho décimas de potencial que nos podría dar alguna posición, aunque ese top-5 era inalcanzable", añadió. Tiempos en mano, todavía existía brecha. "Los veo y el sexto nos saca 1.8. Es demasiado como para pensar en algo más", confesó tras un sábado en el que enseñó lo que ocurre en igualdad de condiciones. "La lluvia nos abrió una oportunidad que aprovechamos. Son circunstancias que ayudan a los que estamos al fondo, y tomamos riesgos desde la Q1 y Q2 en unas condiciones desconocidas para todos. Conseguimos la primera Q3 del año y estoy contento", explicó. Necesita que la carrera siga la misma tónica. "Si llueve, podemos tener una buena oportunidad. Pero será difícil, pues hay coches rápidos detrás. Pero entre la visibilidad y una carrera siempre difícil, nos dará una buena oportunidad de sumar puntos que con otras condiciones. Estábamos 18º en el libre 3, y sufríamos más de lo que creíamos", avanzó. Obviamente, con agua incide menos la unidad de potencia Honda. "Hay menos tiempo con el pedal a fondo porque no hay adherencia, así que los demás no pueden aprovechar ese extra de potencia. Pero el motor es importante para la manejabilidad y el comportamiento en curvas, y allí tenemos problemas. Además, hay aquaplanning y tienes que arriesgarte para clasificarte", cerró.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton reveals details of talks with Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc in Brazil after Mexico fall out
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc held talks with Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur in Brazil following their contentious opening lap incident last time out in Mexico; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm
articles.body:
Hamilton, Leclerc and team principal Frederic Vasseur held talks on Thursday night to discuss the incident which saw Max Verstappen take advantage of the opening lap Ferrari squabble last Sunday to win the race.

Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future.

Hamilton will start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix due to a power unit change and spoke to the media for the first time on Saturday since his talks with Leclerc.

"Me and Charles sat and spoke and we squashed it, and we're moving on," he told Sky Sports F1 .

"We still have a huge amount of respect for each other and I'm glad we had a chat and now we move on.

"We've been getting along just fine as normal. Sometimes in those scenarios it takes having a conversation and there's been no demands from either side, it's both just giving our points and areas we can do better and support each other. I'm hoping to have better races moving forwards."

Leclerc, who starts 14th after a 10-grid place penalty for a new internal combustion engine, had a similar opinion to Hamilton.

"Obviously, there's been a lot of things, probably too much things in the last week," he said.

"We've spoken. I think everything is settled, and I'm looking forward for the rest of the weekend now."

Vasseur: The guidelines are still the same

The Mexico incident comes two months after Leclerc admitted he was at fault for his opening lap battle with Hamilton in Monza, where the latter was forced wide into the gravel and lost several positions.

Vasseur says he reminded Hamilton and Leclerc that the team comes first and the drivers must "keep that in mind".

"The guidelines are still the same. They accumulated perhaps a bit of frustration because they are starting each weekend side by side, and you have a kind of accumulation of fact," he said.

"But at the end of the day, the guideline is always the same - it's that they need to respect each other.

"They are two competitors with the fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have a respect for the other one.

"But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working at the on track.

"I think we are putting a lot of effort on this, and the message was clear and will stay clear."

articles.title: George Russell: 'Very disappointed' Mercedes driver says team error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole in chaotic wet qualifying
articles.summary: George Russell was beaten to pole for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix by Lando Norris; Russell believes Mercedes' instruction for him to abort a flying lap cost him pole; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm
articles.body:
Russell drove impressively throughout a hugely-challenging wet qualifying session at Interlagos but ultimately missed out on pole position by two tenths to McLaren's Lando Norris.

The Mercedes driver had led Norris by four tenths of a second after their first runs in Q3, but was then told to abort his second run when he was being held up by the Williams of Alex Albon.

Mercedes thought that Russell would have time to complete another push lap, but the rain intensified moments later and prevented anyone from going faster for the seven minutes of the session that remained.

Russell reacted with fury over team radio, questioning the instruction for him to abort and insisting that regardless of the time he was losing behind Albon, he would have been able to better Norris' time.

As Russell is serving a five-place grid penalty in Brazil for taking a new internal combustion engine, he would not have started from pole in any case, and will now begin Sunday's race in seventh.

"I think it was just a bit of miscommunication," Russell said. "I need to speak with the team because we believed we'd get another lap before the rain came in.

"So, I was on a really strong lap and I was asked to back off because I caught up Albon, and then obviously the rain came.

"So, yeah, it was very disappointing. I need to understand how it happened and why we got that wrong.

"But I felt very strong, the whole session. Similar to Lando, I had more confidence in the wet than I had in the dry. But yeah, I definitely felt pole was there for the taking."

Asked whether he considered overriding the instruction to abort his lap, Russell added: "They've got the weather forecast in front of them and I don't. And this is where you need that trust and you're relying on one another.

"Obviously, it was the wrong decision, and it was a decision that I think, as soon as it was made, I think we knew it was the wrong one because already they could actually feel the rain pouring harder."

Despite his clear frustration, Russell insisted his race engineer Marcus Dudley, along with other colleagues, weren't necessary responsible given the decision would have been led by the information they were seeing.

"We need to understand, we're relying on a lot of systems. We can't point the finger at somebody," Russell said.

"We need to understand why we made that decision and were our systems telling us what we needed to know because you're relying on the radar.

"But it doesn't make it any less frustrating for me. It's not my engineer's fault. He's relaying information.

"He's ultimately the one who passes the message on. But he's got 12 people talking to him, giving him that information to relay on, so we just need to understand why we made that decision."

Wolff unsure Russell would have got pole with aborted lap

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said he didn't think Russell would have been able to beat Norris to pole on the aborted lap due to the time his driver was losing behind Albon.

"If we were to have a crystal ball to know whether you should back off or not, that would be helpful," Wolff told Sky Sports F1 .

"It was a difficult one, a 50-50 call. He was running into Albon.

"He was 18 milliseconds up on Norris at that stage. I don't think it would have been enough for pole, but he drove perfectly all session and merited to be on pole.

"He deserved it but you can't make that call. It's 50 per cent right or wrong. George was in a league of his own today."

Russell's frustrations follow his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who qualified third, being crowned world champion at last weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix.

The Brit was excused from his media duties after the race in Mexico as Wolff described him as "distraught", with Russell revealing in Brazil that he had found the situation hard to deal with, especially after a technical issue saw him drop back from second on the grid on the opening lap.

As Russell expressed his anger at the instruction to abort the lap in Brazil, Wolff came on the radio in an apparent attempt to diffuse the situation as he told his driver second was a strong result.

Asked for his feelings on Wolff's radio communication with him, Russell said he understood that the Austrian was attempting to protect the wider morale of the team.

"When you're a driver, you're the one who feels it the most," Russell said. "And going back to his (Wolff's) leadership skills, we've got to remember, we collectively made a misjudgement today, and there's members of my team who are going to be feeling as bad as I am currently.

"So, it's important to remember that and we need to just keep the morale high.

"It was a very solid performance, and I guess we take the positive from that. There are no points for a pole, but it would have just been a nice little one to add to the tally."

Sky Sports pundits Karun Chandhok and Bernie Collins were split on whether Russell would have claimed pole had he completed the lap behind Albon.

Chandhok said: "In George's mind, he felt like he should have carried on.

"I don't think he would have beaten Lando to be honest. He was so close to Alex and would have had to follow him. I don't know if he would have got pole.

"I can see the frustration but personally, I think he would have lost more time being stuck behind Albon and I don't think he would have beaten Lando."

But Collins said: "I can see why he's disappointed.

"I think he would have been on pole on that second lap because his fastest first and second sector, with Albon's fastest third sector is enough for pole.

"His middle sector on that lap was actually seven tenths up."

articles.title: Sao Paulo GP: Can Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton come from the back again as Lando Norris hopes for rain to fight Kimi Antonelli
articles.summary: Lando Norris starts on pole in Brazil from Kimi Antonelli but there will be plenty of attention further down the field with Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton starting at the back; watch Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix live at 5pm on Sky Sports F1, build-up from 3.30pm
articles.body:
For the third year in a row, Lando Norris will start on pole position in Brazil with new F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli alongside him on the front row.

Unusually though, there will be plenty of attention further down the field as power unit changes for Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton mean they start at the back, while Ferrari's Charles Leclerc starts 14th for a 10-grid place penalty.

And Mercedes' George Russell, who was left frustrated to not qualify first after a strategic error from the team, starts seventh following a five-place grid penalty for a new internal combustion engine, so several of F1's biggest names will begin the Sao Paulo Grand Prix - lights out at 5pm on Sunday with build-up from 3.30pm, live on Sky Sports F1 - out of position.

"It's almost a reverse grid race, no?" Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1 .

"Yeah, exciting. I think we want to lock in the points for the Constructors' Championship. But it's all floodgates open, the better. Let's race."

How far can Verstappen and Hamilton climb up the field?

Verstappen is no stranger to making his way through the pack at Interlagos after his remarkable victory from 17th in 2024 in the rain.

The Red Bull driver, who has won three times in Brazil, gained 11 places in the opening 11 laps before making the right strategy call to take a crucial victory.

Last year, Verstappen started from the pit lane and impressively charged his way to the podium in dry conditions, but he thinks it will be more difficult to get towards the front this time around.

"It's going to be a bit harder to overtake. The Overtake Mode doesn't really do a lot around here. Everyone is draining their battery from the last corner to Turn 1. Everyone has their wings open, so the effect is less than normal," he told Sky Sports F1 .

"That will make it a bit harder to overtake once you get to the cars that are similar on lap times. The first few cars are not a problem. The others will be a little harder."

Hamilton memorably went from 20th to fifth in the 2021 Sprint in Brazil, after he was disqualified from Qualifying, then won the Grand Prix after starting 10th.

However, Hamilton will not have the same car advantage from five years ago with Ferrari struggling this weekend compared to their recent form.

But, the high chance of rain means Hamilton, and Verstappen, will have the chance to showcase their extraordinary skill and could still find themselves towards the pointy end of the field with a special performance.

"It will be tricky conditions but I love racing in the rain," said Hamilton.

"I was basically using the qualifying as a test to make sure the engine is working, and making sure the car felt good. I feel good for tomorrow."

Leclerc has less cars to overtake from 14th and feels he learned a lot from the wet qualifying by experimenting with set-up tweaks which will benefit him in the race.

"It's going to be very tricky. My biggest strength in the junior categories has been wet driving. Since my nine years with Ferrari, we have never found a way around it," he told Sky Sports F1 .

"I still believe if we manage to find the right window of this car, we can fight for much better than top six."

Norris hoping for 'dark, gloomy day' to fight Antonelli

Perhaps quite fittingly, last year's F1 world champion Norris will start on pole from the new world champion Antonelli in the first race since the latter secured this year's title a week ago in Mexico.

McLaren have brought a new front wing, rear wing, beam wing and floor elements to their car this weekend and it appears to have made an immediate performance impact.

Norris and Antonelli traded lap times throughout Friday's practice sessions in the dry but the McLaren driver feels he needs rain to beat Antonelli on Sunday.

"I expect a battle no matter what. If it's dry, I probably expect a bigger battle because I don't think we quite have the speed compared to them," he told Sky Sports F1 .

"That's why I feel like we had a very good day today. We made the most of conditions where it's not so much about who has the best car, it's more who can push things to the limit and make the most of that opportunity.

"I'm hoping when I wake up it's a dark, gloomy day because we will have a better chance then."

Norris pointed to Antonelli's impressive long run pace in the dry on Friday as the reason he's hoping for rain, whereas the Mercedes driver says he's open to any conditions.

"Hopefully, we can get off the line well, and let's see if it's going to be wet or dry," said Antonelli.

"In the dry, I felt very good over a single lap and on the long run, especially in FP2. So let's see. I'm looking forward to it.

Mercedes have a big opportunity to win the Constructors' Championship with Antonelli starting in second and Russell in seventh, while the two Ferraris are outside of the top 13.

If Mercedes outscore Ferrari by three points, or more, they will seal their ninth title since 2014 but the result of the race itself appears to be more important to the drivers, and Russell is hoping for more rain following his impressive qualifying.

"I felt really confident in the rain. I think my pace, along with Lando's, was by far the best out there," he said

"In the rain here, it's always a challenge. I hope it is wet. I feel I've got a greater chance if it's wet."

articles.title: Sao Paulo Grand Prix: Lando Norris and George Russell hoping for more rain in race after wet qualifying
articles.summary: Polesitter Lando Norris says qualifying for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix brought "some of the wettest conditions" in which he had ever driven.
articles.body:
Lando Norris says qualifying for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix brought "some of the wettest conditions" in which he had ever driven - and he is hoping for more rain in the race on Sunday.

It was the third consecutive year in which Norris has taken pole in Brazil, and it came in a session that was stopped for nearly an hour and a half because conditions were too dangerous to continue when officials initially tried to start it.

Many drivers agreed that conditions were borderline in the extreme.

Mercedes driver George Russell, who qualified second to Norris and was miffed about a team miscommunication that he felt robbed him of pole, said: "Q1 was extremely challenging. The visibility was zero down the straight into Turn Four. I was wheel-spinning in fifth gear, over 200km/h (120mph), aquaplaning.

"When you're aquaplaning on the straight and you can't see in front of you, it's... I'm not even sure what the word is to describe it.

"It does seem a bit crazy. I guess that's what we have to deal with.

"I love driving in the rain. I love driving in the rain here, but at some point, if that was a race, there was no way we should be driving in that because the chances of seeing a really, really horrific incident are very, very high."

The rain - combined with grid penalties for four of the usual front-runners, including Russell - has produced an unfamiliar grid with several drivers exploiting the opportunity of the weather to produce their best results of the year.

Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson - who still does not know whether he has a seat next year - and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg occupy the second row.

Haas driver Oliver Bearman is sixth, and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso and Williams' Alex Albon in eighth and ninth both made it into the top 10 for the first time in 2026.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Red Bull's Max Verstappen, who won this race in the wet two years ago from 17th on the grid, start 20th and 21st after replacing their engines and exceeding their allowance for the year.

Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc, who qualified fourth, has a 10-place penalty, also for engine usage.

Sunday's forecast is for light rain, and the unpredictability of the weather at the Interlagos track, which is famous for it, means the teams and drivers will be open-minded about what to expect.

Norris takes pole in rain-delayed qualifying

Hamilton & Verstappen to start from back in Brazil

Norris had not taken pole since the Spanish Grand Prix in September, and although his McLaren has upgrades on it, which he acknowledged had improved the car, he felt he owed it to the conditions.

"We're lucky it's wet, because if it was dry, I wouldn't be sitting here," said Norris. "In the dry, we definitely didn't have the pace.

"We've looked better this weekend but we still had some small issues, and we've not been up to the pace of the Mercedes. The wet kind of gave me an opportunity and I made the most of it.

"I'm hoping for a wet race. There's a good likelihood it'll be wet. There's a bit of rain, I think, tomorrow at times, and it'll still be damp through the day, so we could just have an exciting race with a little bit of everything, honestly.

"These are conditions where you feel like you can make a little bit more of a difference at times, for sure. And I feel like I'm against good guys who also have the capabilities of going for pole, and today we managed to do it because I put two good laps together and I had a good gap, and we managed things well.

"It was tense when you want to push so much. You need to kind of learn about the conditions, but you also need to not make a single mistake.

"But actually, I felt pretty confident through the whole of qualifying. Q3 was definitely the trickiest because it was also difficult to see, because of the light, where were the dry bits, the wet bits and puddles, things like that. So, more rewarding."

Russell reminds himself 'I haven't forgotten how to drive'

For Russell, there was another disappointment in a season that has been full of them.

Last weekend, he had to watch team-mate Kimi Antonelli clinch the world title and become the youngest champion in history.

Here, he felt pole was his had he not been told to back off on what he felt would have been his fastest lap after he came across Albon in the twisty middle sector.

The team felt the imminent heavier rain would hold off long enough for him to do another lap. They were wrong, and Russell swore over the radio asking what had happened.

He was reminded by team boss Toto Wolff that he was still P2, to which he responded, short-tempered, that he was not there to be second.

It might have seemed a loss of perspective, given his five-place grid penalty meant he would not have been on pole even if he had been fastest.

But for Russell his feelings were rooted in self-validation after a difficult year, and it was not related to the fact that it promoted Antonelli to second.

"Gives me the confidence and reminds me again that I haven't forgotten how to drive," he said. "That's important in circumstances like these and it would have meant a lot to me to clinch the pole with a great performance like we showed in qualifying."

He added: "I felt really confident in the rain. I think my pace, along with Lando's, was by far the best out there.

"In the rain here, it's always a challenge. I hope it is wet tomorrow. I feel I've got a greater chance if it's wet."

The wet conditions provided Alonso with a chance to demonstrate the waste of talent that this year's uncompetitive Aston Martin-Honda car has created.

With its down-on-power and difficult engine, Alonso has been struggling all year. There have been few chinks of light.

This was a rare opportunity to shine, and he took it.

Up at the sharp end throughout, he dropped away - if only relatively - in the final session when he could not get temperature in his tyres. It may have been because he was first in the queue in the pit lane in his eagerness to get in a lap time before the rain worsened again.

"We took some risks in Q1, in Q2, where the conditions were a little bit unknown for everybody and we made it through and then our first Q3 of the year, so obviously pleased with that," Alonso said.

"Then in Q3 I was expecting maybe a little bit more. I was first on the queue. But the tyres were ice cold in Q3, so I had no grip.

"But yeah, I look at the times now, I think P6 is 1.8 seconds in front of me. So yeah, it's way too much, you know, in front to really dream about any higher positions.

"There is less time full throttle (in the wet), because there is no grip. So obviously they cannot exploit the extra power.

"But still the engine is very important in terms of drivability and the way it behaves in the corners. We still have a little bit of an issue there.

"But no, I think these conditions is more about the level of risk you want to take. There is a little bit of aquaplaning here and there."

Alonso joins Norris and Russell in hoping for a wet race, feeling that if it's dry he will inevitably sink back to Aston Martin's natural level, especially with the long pit straight where Honda's lack of power will render him defenceless.

Hamilton and Leclerc 'moving on' after talks

The race promises much with Leclerc, Hamilton and Verstappen all aiming to make progress from the back, even if the drivers feel that overtaking at Interlagos will be harder in this year's new-style cars than before.

For Ferrari, it has been a difficult weekend, that started with clear-the-air talks between Leclerc and Hamilton after their first-lap battle cost them victory in Mexico last weekend.

Both took new internal combustion engines, which gave them 10-place grid penalties, and then Hamilton's brand new one broke in final practice. So Ferrari gave him another one, leaving him at the back with Verstappen.

The two multiple champions will be in competition to see who can make progress faster, and perhaps Ferrari are not so unhappy that Hamilton and Leclerc are separated by six places on the grid.

Both drivers said all was well after their chat on Thursday evening.

Leclerc - who returned to Europe between the two races to be at the birth of his first child, a daughter named Bianca - said: "It was good to speak. This is always needed after a moment like this. It took proportions that are way too big, but it has been around also for way too long.

"At the same time, it was a very special week for me, so I couldn't really have those discussions before. And it was important to have those discussions, but now I consider that a closed chapter, and it will be important to look ahead.

"I really believe that when we speak, things are much better straight away. Of course, there is tension. Of course, we want to finish ahead of each other, and sometimes we are not going to do things right. And it's OK sometimes to disagree on the way you see things, but at the same time, discussing about those then helps a whole lot."

Hamilton added: "Me and Charles sat and spoke and we squashed it, and we're moving on.

"We still have a huge amount of respect for each other and I'm glad we had a chat and now we move on.

"We've been getting along just fine as normal. Sometimes in those scenarios it takes having a conversation and there's been no demands from either side.

"It's both just giving our points and areas we can do better and support each other."

articles.title: La reacción de Aprilia al toque de Marc Márquez: de los aplausos del jefe al "cosas que pasan" de Bezzecchi
articles.standfirst: Rivola, irónico y Bezzecchi se contiene
articles.summary: Rivola, irónico y Bezzecchi se contiene
articles.body: En el box de Aprilia se oía un sonoro 'Noooo' después del toque entre Marc Márquez y Marco Bezzecchi en el Sprint de MotoGP del Gran Premio de Qatar, en Lusail. El lance acabó con el del Ducati oficial sobre su moto y el de Rímini por los suelos. Posteriormente, los comisarios anunciaron que no habría sanción por parte de los comisarios. Esto provocó unos aplausos irónicos del jefe, Massimo Rivola, CEO de Aprilia Racing, como captaron las cámaras. De este modo hacía evidente su desacuerdo con la falta de penalización para el ilerdense. Más tarde, 'Bez' se contenía mucho al valorar todo. “La primera salida ha sido muy positiva, porque he salido bien, me he puesto delante y la carrera estaba yendo bien. Luego, hemos tenido la bandera roja. La segunda salida no ha sido tan perfecta. Desafortunadamente, no hemos salido muy bien y estaba segundo. Estaba yendo todo bien. Ha sido una bonita pelea hasta el contacto. Al final, qué quieres que diga. He tratado de hacer mi línea, desafortunadamente, nos hemos tocado y el que se ha caído he sido yo. Trataremos de intentarlo mañana”, decía en DAZN. El italiano prefería no mojarse sobre si se debía haber castigado a Marc Márquez por el lance. “Esto no es algo que sea me atañe a mí. Yo piloto, vosotros podéis ver las imágenes y juzgar como queráis, pero, al final, yo me dedico a pilotar la moto y respeto las decisiones de Dirección de Carrera, que son quienes deciden”, aseguró. El transalpino trataba de explicar por qué no acaban de llegar algunos resultados pese a su gran velocidad. "Al final, en Malasia no estábamos en disposición de luchar por la victoria, porque no teníamos la velocidad, pero es verdad que en el pasado he sido bastante rápido, también aquí. Desafortunadamente, son cosas de las carreras, pueden pasar. Es verdad que tenemos que mejorar y buscar mejorar algunos detalles, pero, al final, hay cosas que, simplemente, pueden ocurrir en las carreras como, quizá, es lo que ha ocurrido hoy. A continuar trabajando, no tirar la toalla y tratar de ir construyendo mejores sensaciones y conexiones con la moto, más de todo. Tratar de ir siempre más rápido y luego ya llegarán, seguro, cosas positivas”, expuso. Bezzecchi, eso sí, se nota fuerte para la prueba dominical. “La verdad es que he trabajado bien todo el fin de semana con todo el equipo, soy bastante rápido y, como se vio, también hoy podía haber sido más rápido, pero ha ido la cosa así. Trataremos de mantener la concentración, hacer un buen trabajo y mañana veremos”, cerró. Fabio Di Giannantonio, que estaba tras ambos en el toque dio su opinión. “Siempre es muy feo cuando un piloto se cae delante de ti. Es muy difícil, siempre es una cosa muy en el borde. Tenemos comisarios ahí que deciden, yo sólo sentí miedo al tener a Bezzecchi ahí delante de mí”, dijo en DAZN.

articles.title: Hamilton y Leclerc: alto en fuego
articles.standfirst: La guerra en Ferrari vivió su momento más tenso en México y tras varias reuniones en Brasil puede llegar a un punto de encuentro
articles.summary: La guerra en Ferrari vivió su momento más tenso en México y tras varias reuniones en Brasil puede llegar a un punto de encuentro
articles.body: No será, teóricamente, el Gran Premio de Brasil (18:00 horas, DAZN) más sencillo para Ferrari. Sí que en tiempos recientes ha disfrutado en Interlagos, con su último título de 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) y buenas oportunidades en 2008 (Felipe Massa) o 2012 (Fernando Alonso), pero en 2026 partirán desde lejos. Charles Leclerc sale 14º tras sufrir una penalización de 10 posiciones y Lewis Hamilton lo hará 20º después de acumular dos sanciones al cambiar por completo la unidad de potencia. El triunfo apunta a la cabeza, con Lando Norris y Kimi Antonelli con ventaja tras la clasificación bajo la lluvia. Pero para Ferrari hay otros asuntos importantes. Uno deportivo será alargar un título de constructores que se le escapa, otro, y el principal, es calmar las aguas en su box. La guerra desde el verano entre Hamilton y Leclerc es total, y en México alcanzó su punto álgido con cruce de declaraciones, roce en pista y una victoria regalada a Max Verstappen cuando la tenían a tiro. Entre los pilotos el clima no es positivo, y es casi un asunto de estado entre la dirigencia de Maranello, los aficionados y el sentir del propio equipo. Tras el sábado, esa marejada pareció calmarse. Hamilton cambió su discurso y lo moderó. Quizá influyó la reunión con el jefe, Fred Vasseur, o un juego que va más allá de lo que se ve delante de las cámaras. Pero el heptacampeón tiró de cordialidad. "Charles y yo nos sentamos a hablar, lo solucionamos y hemos pasado página. Tenemos un enorme respeto mutuo", precisó el británico. Que cree en un acuerdo sin fisuras. "No han existido exigencias. Señalamos nuestros puntos de vista y en qué podemos mejorar para ayudarnos mutuamente", agregó. Hamilton, además, apunta a una buena relación. "Nos seguimos llevando tan bien como siempre", lanzó. Cosa que Leclerc confirma: "La conversación entre todos tenía que ocurrir. Hemos hablado calmadamente, dijimos lo que pensábamos y nos ha calmado. No quiero detallar más ni incidir en algo que ya ha quedado muy lejos". La guerra... ha llegado a un alto en fuego. Porque quizá las paces todavía no han quedado del todo demostradas, más con dos personalidades llamadas a volver a encontrarse. En Brasil puede ser un caso o tarde o temprano como dice su carrera deportiva. La de Hamilton no lleva a equívocos, y el pasado de Leclerc habla por si sólo. Aunque les ayudará si no hacen todo tan explícito con la radio en medio.

articles.title: A qué hora es la carrera de F1 del GP de Brasil: horario, parrilla y dónde ver en TV a Alonso y Sainz
articles.summary: Alonso volvió a ser 'MAGIC'
articles.body: Una 'pole' magistral de Lando Norris bajo la lluvia de Interlagos en la que el de McLaren supo ser el más fino para lograr llevarse la primera posición con intermedios, seguido de George Russell y del Campeón del Mundo, Kimi Antonelli. Tras una sesión muy retrasada, finalmente los pilotos pudieron saltar a pista a "sobrevivir" e intentar rascar la mejor posición posible. Y fue precisamente lo que hizo Fernando Alonso, quien volvió a hacernos partícipes del talento innato que tiene, se convirtió en 'Magic' y no sólo logró pasar a Q3, sino que acabó clasificando 9º, el cual se convertirá en un 8º puesto debido a la sanción de Leclerc, 10 posiciones y quien clasificó 4º. Mientras que Alonso obraba el milagro, Carlos Sainz volvió a ser víctima de la mala suerte. El madrileño, que había logrado pasar a la Q2, no pudo dar esa última vuelta que le diera una última oportunidad de pasar a Q3, debido a un accidente de Câmara y con el que acabó antes de los previsto la sesión al salir la bandera roja. Así pues, el de Williams tendrá que partir desde la 15ª posición, rezando para que llueva y sus posibilidades puedan aumentar. Como es habitual, el Gran Premio de Brasil de Fórmula 1 2026 se podrá ver en directo por televisión a través de DAZN F1 y en Movistar+. También tienes la opción de seguir todo lo que suceda en la carrera en Sao Paulo a través de los directos de MARCA.com y la transmisión de la carrera en Radio MARCA. articles.summary: El '93' tiene la primera oportunidad de cerrar el título
articles.body: Marc Márquez está a un paso de volver a convertirse en Campeón del Mundo, tan sólo una victoria y ningún punto por parte de Jorge Martín para que 10º sea suyo. Sin embargo, sabe que lo tiene muy complicado. El de Ducati firmó su 25ª victoria al Sprint desde que existe el formato, siendo el que más tiene de la historia. Le siguió Fabio Di Giannantonio, quien logró adelantar finalmente en la última vuelta a Jorge Martín, el cuál quedó 3º tras un heroico sábado, en el que 'hizo de tripas corazón, aguantó el dolor y logró subir al pódium tras una carrera bastante movida, en la que su compañero de equipo, Marco Bezzecchi, se fue al suelo tras un toque con el líder del Mundial, Marc Márquez. En la categoría intermedia, Manu González resurgió de sus cenizas y logró un segundo puesto en parrilla, tras Álex Escrig, que, sumado a la 7ª posición de su máximo rival por el Mundial, Izan Guevara, dan una oportunidad de oro al madrileño para aumentar algo de esa ventaja que ha estado perdiendo las últimas carreras. Dani Holgado cierra la primera fila. El Campeón del Mundo no se cansa de ser primero. Ya que no puede superar el récord de David Alonso, al menos Máximo Quiles tratará de igualarlo. El murciano ha logrado firmar otra 'pole' más y mañana buscará la victoria 12 de la temporada. Al '28' le siguen David Almansa y Brian Uriarte. articles.title: Honda F1 celebra la hazaña de Alonso
articles.standfirst: "Es nuestro mejor resultado con Aston Martin y de todo el año; esperamos más lluvia para la carrera"
articles.summary: "Es nuestro mejor resultado con Aston Martin y de todo el año; esperamos más lluvia para la carrera"
articles.body: El ingeniero jefe de Honda F1, Shintaro Orihara, realizaba una evaluación de lo vivido el sábado en Interlagos, primero en los libres 3 en seco y luego en la calificación vespertina, con lluvia por cada rincón de la sesión, que iba variando en intensidad. "Durante la tercera sesión de entrenamientos libres (FP3) del Gran Premio de Sao Paulo, surgió otro problema con el ERS (sistema de recuperación de energía) en el coche de Lance Stroll; ahora enviaremos la pieza a HRC Sakura para su inspección. Gracias al esfuerzo conjunto de nuestro personal en el circuito y del resto del equipo, logramos que Lance pudiera salir a pista durante la sesión de clasificación", valoraba sobre el compañero de Alonso, que quedó eliminado en Q1, pese a tener el coche en las mismas condiciones. "Preparamos la configuración de nuestra unidad de potencia para condiciones de lluvia, basándonos en la previsión meteorológica, lo cual dio sus frutos dadas las condiciones que se presentaron durante la clasificación. En ambos monoplazas, implementamos ajustes específicos en la gestión de la energía para favorecer la manejabilidad bajo la lluvia intensa. Algunos aspectos funcionaron bien, pero todavía quedan ajustes por realizar para seguir mejorando", explicaba sobre las modificaciones realizadas tras la experiencia de Sepang, fundamentalmente. "En cuanto a Fernando, comenzaremos el gran premio desde la octava posición de la parrilla... Es nuestro mejor resultado del año y el mejor desde que comenzó nuestra colaboración con el equipo Aston Martin Aramco Fórmula 1", constataba Orihara. Ese octavo de parrilla estuvo precedido de un séptimo en Q2, en la que dejóa a Hamilton y a Piastri por detrás de su AMR26. En realidad, es el mejor resultado en una cronometrada de sábado, pues en carrera fue mucho más difícil acabar octavo en Malasia, dejando detrás al McLaren de Norris durante las tres últimas vueltas. "Fernando siempre pesca en estas carreras", confesaba Lando tras pasar la bandera a cuadros. "Esperamos más lluvia para la carrera, así que en Honda estaremos preparados a partir de lo que hemos aprendido", cerraba. Otro milagro es posible, porque la jornada amenaza llovizna y pista resbaladiza para toda la jornada de este domingo.
